split_strategy.rationale: The data are a time series observed on a fixed station network. A random split would let the model see a July 2024 afternoon while predicting the hour beside it, which no deployed system could do.

data_sources.name: NOAA NCEI Integrated Surface Database (ISD-Lite)
data_sources.license: U.S. Government work — public domain (NOAA open data)
data_sources.description: Quality-controlled hourly surface weather observations from physical stations: air temperature, dew point, sea-level pressure, wind, sky cover and precipitation.

data_sources.name: NOAA NCEI ISD Station History
data_sources.license: U.S. Government work — public domain (NOAA open data)
data_sources.description: Station inventory: identifiers, coordinates, elevation, period of record.

data_sources.name: OpenStreetMap via Overpass API
data_sources.description: Building footprints, road network, green space and water bodies used to derive urban-morphology features around each station.

data_sources.name: NYISO Real-Time Actual Load (Palisades archive)
data_sources.license: NYISO public market information — free public use
data_sources.description: Real-time metered electricity load for the 11 NYISO load zones.

data_sources.name: Open-Meteo Elevation API (Copernicus DEM GLO-90)
data_sources.description: Digital-elevation lookup used to sanity-check station elevations.

split.thinning: Windows larger than their cap are thinned by a regular stride through time; every model is scored on identical rows.
